reader.requirement: END-START must end the scope of a relative-file START, so the statements after it belong to the enclosing statement (IF, PERFORM, another START's INVALID KEY phrase) whether or not INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY is written; an END-START with no START to close must be refused, and the 1985 START format (KEY phrase only) must refuse a later edition's FIRST/LAST.

edition-consulted.switches: START FIRST/LAST refused below 2002 (COBOL0900, Constructs.StartFirstLast2002); the END-START scope is not gated
ctx.Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands for the KEY operand; not the scope terminator

reader.edition-search: grep END_START over the grammar (CobolIO.g4 startStatement, CobolLexer.g4) and VersionConformancePass/FlagConformancePass for StartStatement: the terminator is plain grammar with no edition predicate.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb333_start_general_relation_operators uses END-START with INVALID KEY at top level; nesting inside IF, inline PERFORM, another START's phrase, END-START with no conditional phrase and a stray END-START are not exercised

probes.printed: T1 INVALID / T1 AFTER-START (in IF then-branch); T2 NOT-INVALID / T2 AFTER-START; T3 OUTER-INVALID / T3 INNER-OK / T3 OUTER-CONTINUES / T3 DONE; USE RAN ST=23 / T4 ST=23 (END-START with no phrase, USE applies); T5 INVALID / T5 IN-PERFORM ST=23
probes.expected: each END-START closes only its own START; the following statement runs inside the enclosing statement

reader.notes: startStatement ends in END_START? after conditionalPhrases, so the explicit terminator closes the innermost open START and the parser hands the following statements to the enclosing construct.
